Two changes. One removes duplicated external verification; one marks a finished experiment as finished.

## 1 — AXLE mutation deduplication

`tests/test_correspondence.py` builds a worktree, edits **one** file under `src/`, and runs `correspondence_gate.py`. That gate globs `src/*.py` (`correspondence_gate.py:99-102`) and makes **one AXLE kernel call per source** (`correspondence_gate.py:312`) — so a test that changed one function re-proved four.

### Counted, not estimated

Two tests in this file build a worktree and run the gate. A third calls `axle()` once directly and is unaffected. The rest never run the gate.

|  | calls |
|---|---|
| `AXLE_CALLS_BEFORE` | 2 × 4 + 1 = **9** |
| `AXLE_CALLS_AFTER` | 2 × 1 + 1 = **3** |
| removed | **6** |

**Removed:** repeated verification of groups the test proved nothing about.
**Not removed:** any AXLE call, Lean proof, or verdict for the mutated group.

> An earlier draft of this PR said 42 → 13, carried from a plan that assumed thirteen worktree-building tests when there are two. The GitHub measurement caught it — see the correction commit. Twenty-nine removed calls could not have cost eight seconds.

### Measured on GitHub, same verdicts

| run | result | axle suite |
|---|---|---|
| before — `8ea48f36`, run `32371336445` | `13 passed, 767 deselected` | **22.27s** |
| after — `e3dc1e3`, run `32374048401` | `13 passed, 772 deselected` | **14.17s** |

Same 13 tests, same verdicts. 8.10s over six calls is 1.35s each, against an 863ms AXLE health round trip — consistent. The `correspondence` job went **53s / 43s → 32s**; it does not regress. The five extra deselected tests are the new acceptance tests below.

### Why removal and not a cache

A reuse cache would have to match seven identity fields — source hash, config hash, AXLE command, tool version, mutation identity, schema version, verification context — and a wrong hit **reports a verification that never happened**. Not performing redundant work has no such failure mode. There is no cache to go stale because there is no cache.

### Why removing sources is safe

`correspondence_gate.py:192-193` is set equality between `src/*.py` stems and `semantics/specs/*_semantics_spec.lean` stems: it fails on `missing` in one direction and `orphans` in the other. `scope_to()` deletes each source **together with its spec and proof**, so the sets stay equal and COMPLETENESS is still genuinely evaluated rather than skipped.

### Fail closed, twice

- `scope_to()` skips any source whose spec/proof pair is incomplete — a half-present pair is never half-removed.
- `worktree()` scopes nothing at all when the mutated function's own pair is absent, because several tests exist precisely to check that absence.

### Acceptance — proven, and free

Five new tests, **none of which call AXLE**. The call count equals the source count, so counting sources counts calls:

| # | proof | how |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the mutated function is always verified | asserted for all four functions |
| 2 | exactly one source survives scoping | source count == call count |
| 3 | COMPLETENESS sets stay equal | sources == specs == proofs, non-empty |
| 4 | an incomplete pair is never scoped away | delete `multiply`'s proof, assert `multiply` survives |
| 5 | scoped and unscoped reach the same verdict | UNSUPPORTED mutation, refused before the kernel — same layer, same exit code |

Serial throughout. No added external-service concurrency. Ordered markers untouched — `run_gate.py` parses them **by position** to report which verifications never ran.

## 2 — `docs/ci-benchmark.md`

The seven-sample comparison was finished and the document never said so. A reader reaching "Why seven samples and not three" finds justified methodology with no marker that the question is settled — and infers that a benchmark here costs seven commits, seven pushes, seven CI runs during ordinary work.

**Every measurement, sample and median is kept verbatim.** Three header lines were reframed; nothing else was deleted. Added: `STATUS: COMPLETED EXPERIMENT`, the accepted configuration, the normal-development path (one change set → one push → one required run), and the conditions that would justify re-measuring.

Also records the contract position in writing: **182s measured against a 900s target, 718s headroom**. The 93s figure from working notes is withdrawn — it measured a push run and omitted a workflow.
